Kenaitze Indian Tribe

The Kenaitze Indian Tribe identifies its people as the Kahtnuht’ana Dena’ina, People of the Kenai River. The Tribe’s public language and institutional accounts make useful starting points for understanding how teaching, government and community services are connected. They describe a living community across the Kenai Peninsula and beyond.

01

Language in the community’s own terms

The Tribe’s language page places Dena’ina within the larger Dene language group. It identifies the Kenai, or Outer Inlet, dialect with Kahtnuht’ana, People of the Kenai River, and connects that name with the Kenaitze Indian Tribe. This keeps a particular community and dialect visible within the broader language. The page points readers toward the Tribe’s Language Institute, audio dictionary and recordings as teaching resources. Those linked materials are invitations for further learning; this guide has reviewed their description, not their full contents or present learning outcomes.

Read the sources [2] Kenaitze Indian Tribe

02

Institutions that bring learning and services together

The Tribe’s About page describes Kahtnuht’ana Qayeh, its campus in Old Town Kenai, as bringing together government and community services. It records the opening of the Dena’ina Wellness Center in 2014 and an education campus opening for in-person services in 2023. In its account, that education campus houses early learning, youth language and culture, and community education and career training. The page also records a 2025 charter-school partnership focused on Dena’ina language and culture. Read together, these dated developments show how the Tribe presents education as part of its broader community work.
